meta.title: Cigarettes smoked in India per month

prompt: Estimate the number of cigarettes smoked in India per month.

clarifications.answer: Use a multi-level split: age, then urban/rural locality, then gender, since all three drive smoking rates. Ignore under-16.
Start from India's 140 crore population; ages 16-22 are ~10% and 22+ ~60% of it.
Urban smokes more than rural, and men more than women; penetration ranges from ~5% (rural women) to ~60% (urban 22+ men).
Assume per-smoker monthly consumption from ~10 (light) up to ~90 (heavy urban male). Answer in crore cigarettes per month.

common_traps: Applying one smoking rate to the whole adult population instead of splitting by locality and gender.
Forgetting that the 22+ urban-male cell dominates, so a rough age split alone misses most of the volume.
Multiplying smokers by a daily rate but reporting the answer as monthly (or vice versa).

anchors.1: Guesses a number with no smokers-times-consumption structure.
anchors.3: Estimates smokers and consumption but at one blanket rate, not multi-level.
anchors.5: Builds smokers per cell via age-locality-gender penetration, then multiplies by per-smoker consumption.

anchors.3: Splits on one dimension (e.g. age or gender) only.
anchors.5: Splits on age, locality and gender with distinct penetration and consumption per cell.

anchors.1: Loses the crore conversions or the day/month basis; lands far off.
anchors.3: Reaches a number with a slip, landing just outside 900-1600 crore.
anchors.5: Carries the per-cell products and crore math cleanly, landing near 1270 crore per month.

anchors.3: Mentions a check but does not complete it.
anchors.5: Cross-checks that the 22+ urban-male cell dominating the total is consistent with real smoking patterns.
